key_insight: Train parallel speculative draft models by directly minimizing the expected number of decoding rounds, rather than using block-local proxy losses that ignore cross-round coupling.
engineering_relevance: This gives a principled, hyperparameter-free way to improve LLM inference speed by increasing accepted draft length and reducing total verification rounds.
method: Model speculative decoding as a Markov reward process.
Define Expected Decoding Rounds (EDR) to exactly match the expected round count.
Derive an exact temporal-difference gradient and an offline round-count evaluator from target-model rollouts.
evidence_signal: Fine-tuning the drafters DSpark and DFly with EDR improved mean accepted length and beat prior training objectives across nine benchmarks in math, code, and chat.
watch_item: The method depends on target-model rollout data and exact round accounting, so implementation must carefully match the speculative decoding setup used during training and evaluation.
paper_title: Training Parallel Speculative Draft Models by Directly Minimizing Expected Decoding Rounds
